p.i: Hunc ornet omnis fusa circum Copia frugum, & opes benignæ. Insculpe tales dehinc titulos globo. FALLACIS ævi conspicuis fugam, Pietásqui fruges, nec manere Quæ vary[?] rapit aura venti.

main_text.head: XIIII. GAL.
main_text.p: ANTIQVITE', pourquoy as tu donné Le nom de biens aux richesses mõdaines, Puis qu'il n'y a que maux, ennuis & peines, Pour l'homme vain, qui y est adonné? Mais toy, mondain, pourquoy abuses tu, De ce qui est instrument de vertu? Les biens sont mal, à qui des biens abusent. Les biens sont bien, aux bons qui bien en vsent.
main_text.head: LAT.
main_text.p: PRÆSENTIS ævi divitias bonum Haud negligendum cur veteres vocant, Si possidenti, siq; amanti Tot mala, tot pariunt labores? Sed cur vocarent divitias malum: Virtutis ardens quæ studium iuvant? Usum nocebunt nescienti, Quæ bona sunt, bene qui scit uti.

page.notes: The French and Latin verse is set in roman type with italic for the Latin lines; "vsent" and "Vsum" follow the printed u/v usage in the rules. Doubtful readings: "vary[?]" (the word after "Quæ" may be "varij" or a similar form); "Pietásqui" is read from a long-s form and may be misprinted. The top italic block is the end of an earlier poem; its opening is not on this page. The large drop cap "A" in "ANTIQVITE'" is printed as an initial, joined to the word as the rules require.
